title: GTFS Realtime Editor Annotation Schema
description: JSON Schema for realtime.ui.yaml, the companion file that records where each GTFS Realtime field's value comes from and, where a person supplies it, which editor component and validation rules it needs. Keyed by '<Message>.<field>' — the field's own definition, not a path to it, so StopTimeEvent.time is annotated once and both arrival.time and departure.time inherit it.

version.description: Annotation format version. Bump on breaking changes to this schema.

fields.description: Annotations keyed by '<Message>.<field>', where <Message> is the protobuf message that declares the field (e.g. 'Alert.header_text', 'StopTimeEvent.time'). Enums are not keyed here: they have no fields of their own, and their values are shown on whichever field selects them.

propertyNames.description: Key must be '<Message>.<field>': the message in PascalCase, the field in snake_case.

origin.description: Where the value comes from. This is the key difference from the Schedule annotations: a Schedule field is always typed by someone, while most Realtime fields are produced by a machine and have no editor at all. Recording that is what keeps the coverage figure honest. 'operator': A person writes this value in an editor — service alerts, mostly. 'system': Produced by a machine: AVL, the prediction engine, the feed builder. 'derived': Computed from the Schedule feed plus observation, not entered anywhere. 'constant': Fixed for the whole feed and set once in configuration.

component.description: Controlled vocabulary of editor components, required when origin is 'operator' and meaningless otherwise. Extend only when a field genuinely cannot be edited by an existing one.

group.description: Fields sharing a group are edited together as one widget (e.g. Position.latitude + Position.longitude render a single map, TimeRange.start + TimeRange.end a single date range).

references.description: The GTFS *Schedule* field this value must match, as '<file>.<field>'. Realtime identifiers are resolved against the static feed, so this is the join that makes a feed consumable — and the check that catches a route_id no timetable has.

i18n.description: Rider-facing editor labels. Present even for fields no person edits: the label is also what the field is called when a screen or a diagnostic names it.

validation.description: Rules the GTFS Realtime spec requires are ERRORS and may be written in scalar short form. Rules that only encode a Best Practice recommendation, or a check the lab added, MUST use the long form with an explicit severity of 'warning' — encoding a recommendation as an error would reject valid feeds.

required.description: true = always required; false = optional; 'conditional' = the spec's Conditionally Required or Conditionally Forbidden, resolved at runtime from the field's conditions.

unique_in_feed.description: The value must not repeat within one feed message. The Schedule side calls this unique_in_file; a Realtime feed has no files, only one message per fetch.

posix_time.description: The value is POSIX time in *seconds*, not milliseconds. Worth stating: a timestamp in milliseconds is the single most common Realtime producer error, it is syntactically valid, and it puts every prediction about fifty thousand years into the future.

not_stale.description: Longest age, in seconds, the value may have before a consumer should stop trusting it. This is about the feed being fresh, not about a screen degrading — a screen's fallback policy lives in composites.yaml.

enum_from_spec.description: Options come from the enum realtime.yaml declares for this field. Never duplicate enum values here.

empty_means.description: Value an omitted field is equivalent to, where the spec defines one. Protobuf cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'default', so where it matters it has to be written down.

code_list.description: External code list the value must belong to.

after.description: The '<Message>.<field>' this value must not precede, for the two ends of a time range.

bounding_box.description: Advisory geographic check. Regions are not redeclared here — they are read from schedule.ui.yaml, because the national box is a property of the territory and not of the feed. Defaults to a warning: a point outside the box is suspicious, not spec-invalid.

severityWrapper.description: Long form of a rule, used when it is not an ERROR. Rules the GTFS Realtime spec requires are errors; rules that only encode a Best Practice recommendation are warnings and must say so explicitly.

value.description: The rule's value, same shape as its scalar short form.

notice.description: Canonical GTFS Realtime validator rule this mirrors, e.g. 'E001' or 'W001'.
